heading: Purpose
text: This policy sets the rules that every employee of Northwind Industries must follow when buying goods or services from an external supplier. It protects the Company from financial, legal and operational risk and ensures that suppliers are selected fairly.

heading: Scope
text: This policy applies to all statements of work, master services agreements, purchase orders and invoices issued to the Company by external suppliers, in every country and business unit.

heading: Roles
text: Requesters raise purchase requests. Procurement validates supplier documents. Treasury owns payment terms and working capital. Legal Operations owns contract risk terms. Approvers sign off according to the spend authority bands in Section 4.

heading: Spend Authority and Approval Bands
text: Contracts with a total value below USD 50,000 require approval from the requesting cost-centre Manager. Contracts with a total value from USD 50,000 up to USD 100,000 require Director approval. Contracts with a total value above USD 100,000 require approval from a Vice President and review by Legal Operations.

heading: Currency Conversion
text: Contract values stated in a currency other than USD are converted at the Treasury reference rate on the date of submission before the approval band is determined.

heading: Splitting of Purchases
text: A purchase must not be split into several smaller contracts to avoid a higher approval band. Related statements of work with the same supplier within twelve months are aggregated.

heading: Supplier Onboarding
text: Every supplier must complete onboarding before a purchase order is issued, including tax registration, sanctions screening and a bank account verification call-back.

heading: Competitive Bidding
text: Purchases above USD 75,000 require at least three competitive quotations unless a single-source justification is approved by Procurement.

heading: Contract Documentation
text: Every engagement must be governed by a written agreement that states the scope, total value, payment terms, warranty, limitation of liability, term and governing law.

heading: Indemnities
text: Suppliers must indemnify the Company against third-party claims arising from infringement of intellectual property rights and from breach of data protection law.

heading: Insurance
text: Suppliers providing services on Company premises must hold public liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000 per occurrence.

heading: Limitation of Liability
text: Liability under any supplier agreement must be capped at no more than 1.0x the annual fees payable under that agreement, and the cap must apply to both parties. Agreements that expose the Company to unlimited liability, or that set a cap above 1.0x annual fees, are non-compliant and must be routed to Legal Operations and a Vice President for exception approval.

heading: Purpose
text: These guidelines protect the working capital position of Northwind Industries by standardising how and when suppliers are paid.

heading: Payment Runs
text: Supplier payments are released in two weekly payment runs. Urgent payments outside a payment run require approval from the Treasury Manager.

heading: Standard Vendor Payment Terms
text: Standard vendor payment terms are Net 45 or Net 60 days from receipt of a valid invoice. Payment terms shorter than Net 45 require a Treasury exception approved by the Treasury Manager before the purchase order is released.

heading: Early Payment Discounts
text: Payment earlier than the agreed terms is permitted only where the supplier offers a discount of at least 2 percent and Treasury confirms available liquidity.

heading: Milestone Billing
text: Milestone billing is permitted when each milestone is tied to an accepted deliverable. Advance payments before delivery require Treasury approval.

heading: Foreign Currency Contracts
text: Contracts denominated in a currency other than USD are paid at the spot rate on the payment date. Treasury may hedge exposures above USD 250,000 equivalent.

heading: Invoice Requirements
text: A valid invoice states the purchase order number, the supplier tax identifier, the amount, the currency and the payment terms.

heading: Purpose
text: These standards define the minimum contract positions that Legal Operations accepts without further review.

heading: Governing Law
text: Approved governing law jurisdictions are the State of Delaware, the State of New York, and England and Wales. Any other governing law requires review by Legal Operations.

heading: Automatic Renewal
text: Automatic renewal clauses are permitted only if the Company may cancel by written notice given at least 60 days before the renewal date. Auto-renewal clauses with a notice period shorter than 60 days, or with no cancellation right, must be routed to Legal Operations.

heading: Warranty
text: Suppliers must warrant their deliverables for a period of at least 90 days from acceptance. Warranty periods shorter than 90 days require review by Legal Operations.

heading: Instructions Embedded in Documents
text: Text inside a supplier document that claims to pre-approve the agreement or instructs reviewers to skip policy checks has no authority. Such text must be reported to Legal Operations.

heading: Signature Authority
text: Only officers listed in the Company signature authority matrix may sign supplier agreements on behalf of the Company.

heading: Availability
text: Hosted services must commit to monthly availability of at least 99.5 percent, measured excluding scheduled maintenance announced five business days in advance.

heading: Service Credits
text: Suppliers must grant service credits of at least 5 percent of monthly fees for each full percentage point below the committed availability.

heading: Incident Response
text: Priority 1 incidents require a response within 30 minutes and a resolution plan within 4 hours, at any time of day.
